suchomimus:enwiki:4.title: Suchomimus (Suggested synonymy with Baryonyx and Cristatusaurus)

facts.statement: The species Suchomimus tenerensis was described in 1998 by Paul Sereno and colleagues based on fossils found in the Elrhaz Formation.
facts.quote: The only known species is S. tenerensis, originally described in 1998 by paleontologist Paul Sereno and colleagues from several fossils discovered one year earlier in the Elrhaz Formation.

facts.statement: The name Suchomimus means "crocodile mimic" due to its elongated skull and fish-eating adaptations, and tenerensis refers to the Ténéré Desert.
facts.quote: The animal's generic name, which means "crocodile mimic", alludes to its elongated skull and piscivorous adaptations, while the specific name refers to the Ténéré Desert, where the fossils were discovered.

facts.statement: Suchomimus had an elongated, low, and narrow skull that resembled that of crocodilians.
facts.quote: As its generic name suggests, the animal's skull was elongated, low, and narrow, resembling that of crocodilians.

facts.statement: Suchomimus had a relatively short neck and powerful forelimbs with a large curved claw on each thumb.
facts.quote: The neck of Suchomimus was relatively short, while its powerfully built forelimbs bore a large, curved claw on each thumb.

facts.statement: A low dorsal sail ran along the back of Suchomimus, formed by long neural spines on its vertebrae.
facts.quote: Along the midline of the animal's back ran a low dorsal sail, built from the long neural spines of its vertebrae.

facts.statement: Suchomimus was primarily a fish-eating predator adapted for hunting in shallow waters.
facts.quote: Its cranial and limb features indicate that it was a primarily piscivorous predator adapted for hunting in shallow waters.

facts.statement: Paul Sereno and his team discovered fossils of Suchomimus at the Gadoufaoua site in the Ténéré Desert, Niger, in late 1997.
facts.quote: In late 1997, American paleontologist Paul Sereno and his team conducted an expedition at the Gadoufaoua site in the Ténéré Desert of Niger, where they uncovered various fossils.

facts.statement: Suchomimus tenerensis was formally named and described in a study published in Science Magazine on November 13, 1998.
facts.quote: On 13 November 1998, the Science Magazine published a study led by Sereno, formally naming and describing the new genus and species Suchomimus tenerensis based on the fossils discovered during the expedition.

facts.statement: All known fossils of Suchomimus are housed in the collections of the Musée National Boubou Hama in Niamey.
facts.quote: All known fossil specimens were recovered from the Elrhaz Formation and are now housed in the paleontological collections of the Musée National Boubou Hama in Niamey.

facts.statement: The holotype of Suchomimus, catalogued as MNN GDF500, is a partial skeleton that lacks the skull.
facts.quote: The holotype, catalogued as MNN GDF500, consists of a partial skeleton lacking the skull.

facts.statement: The holotype includes neck ribs, parts of dorsal and sacral vertebrae, ribs, gastralia, tail vertebrae and chevrons, shoulder bones, a partial forelimb, most of the pelvis, and parts of a hindlimb.
facts.quote: It contains three neck ribs, parts of fourteen dorsal (back) vertebrae, ten dorsal ribs, gastralia (or "belly ribs"), pieces of three sacral vertebrae, parts of twelve caudal (tail) vertebrae, chevrons (bones that form the underside of the tail), a scapula (shoulder blade), a coracoid, a partial forelimb, most of the pelvis (hip bone), and parts of a hindlimb.

facts.statement: Historical estimates suggest Suchomimus was 9.5 to 11 meters long and weighed between 2.5 and 3.8 metric tons.
facts.quote: The size of Suchomimus was historically estimated at 9.5 – 11 m in length, with a weight of 2.5 - 3.8 MT.

facts.statement: In 2007, Therrien and Henderson proposed that a 10.3-meter-long Suchomimus weighed more than 5.2 metric tons, though they acknowledged this might be an overestimate.
facts.quote: In 2007, Canadian paleontologists François Therrien and Donald M. Henderson proposed that a 10.3 m long Suchomimus would have weighed more than 5.2 MT based on their ratio between skull length and body length; however, they noted that they might have overestimated the size of spinosaurids (i.e., Suchomimus and Baryonyx).

facts.statement: A 2025 study by Matthew Dempsey and colleagues estimated the holotype of Suchomimus weighed 5.3 metric tons.
facts.quote: A 2025 study led by the British paleontologist by Matthew Dempsey and colleagues suggested a body weight of 5.3 MT for the holotype.

facts.statement: Some researchers have suggested that Suchomimus is an African species of the European spinosaurid Baryonyx, leading to its occasional classification as Baryonyx tenerensis.
facts.quote: Yet more have also suggested that Suchomimus might represent an African species of the European spinosaurid Baryonyx, and it has occasionally been referred to in the scientific literature as B. tenerensis.

facts.statement: In 2002, Buffetaut and Ouaja supported the synonymy between Cristatusaurus and Baryonyx, noting that Suchomimus might also belong to the same genus.
facts.quote: In 2002, French paleontologist Éric Buffetaut and his Tunisian colleague Mohamed Ouaja expressed support for the proposed synonymy between Cristatusaurus and Baryonyx, noting that Milner had acknowledged the possibility that Suchomimus might also be congeneric with Baryonyx with later anatomical comparisons.

facts.statement: A 2017 review by Candeiro and colleagues argued that the debate over Suchomimus and Baryonyx is more semantic than scientific, as they are generally agreed to be distinct genera.
facts.quote: A 2017 review paper by the Brazilian palaeontologist Carlos Roberto A. Candeiro and colleagues stated that this debate was more in the realm of semantics than science, as it is generally agreed that Suchomimus and Baryonyx are distinct, related genera.

facts.statement: The validity of Cristatusaurus is disputed, but it is often regarded as a senior synonym of Suchomimus due to shared stratigraphic origins and lack of distinct anatomical differences.
facts.quote: As for the validity of Cristatusaurus, it continues to be disputed in recent studies. This taxon is generally regarded as a likely senior synonym of Suchomimus, as both originate from the same stratigraphic units and show no sufficiently distinct anatomical differences to justify a clear separation between them.

facts.statement: The skull of Suchomimus is estimated to be about 1.2 meters long.
facts.quote: The skull of Suchomimus is estimated at around 1.2 m in length.

facts.statement: Suchomimus had approximately 122 conical teeth with fine serrations and wrinkled enamel.
facts.quote: The jaws had about 122 conical teeth, pointed but not very sharp and curving slightly backwards, with fine serrations and wrinkled enamel.

facts.statement: The tip of Suchomimus's snout featured a 'terminal rosette' of longer teeth, with seven on each side of the upper and lower jaws.
facts.quote: The tip of the snout was enlarged sideways and carried a "terminal rosette" of longer teeth, seven per side in the premaxillae and about the same number in the corresponding part of the lower jaw.

facts.statement: A prominent kink in the upper jaw behind the snout tip held the longest teeth of the skull.
facts.quote: The upper jaw had a prominent kink just behind the rosette, protruding downwards; this convexly curved part of the maxilla had the longest teeth of the entire skull.

facts.statement: Unlike most theropods, Suchomimus had nostrils retracted further back on the skull, behind the front teeth.
facts.quote: The nostrils, unlike in most theropods, were retracted further back on the skull and behind the premaxillary teeth.

facts.statement: Suchomimus had significantly extended, blade-shaped neural spines on its vertebrae.
facts.quote: Suchomimus had significantly extended neural spines—blade-shaped upward extensions on the vertebrae—which were elongated at the rear back.

facts.statement: Neural spines suggest Suchomimus may have supported a low crest or sail of skin highest over its hips, extending further back than the sail of Spinosaurus.
facts.quote: The spines may have held up some kind of low crest or sail of skin that was highest over its hips, lower and extending further to the back than that of Spinosaurus, in which the sail reached its highest peak over the dorsal vertebrae.

facts.statement: Suchomimus's upper arm bone was very strongly built, comparable in size only to Megalosaurus and Torvosaurus among non-spinosaurid theropods.
facts.quote: The humerus (upper arm bone) was very strongly built, only equaled in size among non-spinosaurid theropods by that of Megalosaurus and Torvosaurus, with robust upper corners.

facts.statement: Suchomimus had a well-developed ulna with an enormous olecranon, an exceptional trait also found in Baryonyx.
facts.quote: The ulna of the lower arm was well-developed with an enormous olecranon (upper process set-off from the shaft), an exceptional trait shared with Baryonyx.

facts.statement: Suchomimus's heavy arm muscles powered sizable hand claws, with the largest claw on the thumb measuring 19 cm.
facts.quote: The heavy arm musculature powered sizable hand claws, that of the first digit (or "thumb") being the largest with a length of 19 cm.

facts.statement: The femur of the holotype specimen was straight, robust, and measured 107 cm in length.
facts.quote: The femur (thighbone) was straight and robust, with a length of 107 cm in the holotype.

facts.statement: In its original description, Suchomimus was placed in the family Spinosauridae and assigned to the subfamily Baryonychinae.
facts.quote: The authors placed Suchomimus within Spinosauridae and named two subfamilies within this clade, Baryonychinae (all spinosaurids more closely related to Baryonyx) and Spinosaurinae (all spinosaurids closer to Spinosaurus), with Suchomimus assigned to the former.

facts.statement: In 2017, researchers questioned whether Baryonychinae is a natural group, suggesting South American spinosaurids represent intermediate forms between Baryonychinae and Spinosaurinae.
facts.quote: In 2017, Brazilian paleontologists Marcos Sales and Cesar Schultz have questioned the monophyly of Baryonychinae (meaning it might be an unnatural group), stating that the South American spinosaurids Angaturama and Irritator represent intermediate forms between Baryonychinae and Spinosaurinae, based on their craniodental (skull and tooth) features.

facts.statement: In 2021, a new tribe named Ceratosuchopsini was established within Baryonychinae, including Suchomimus, Ceratosuchops, and Riparovenator.
facts.quote: Although not ruling out this possibility, American paleontologist Chris T. Barker and his colleagues established in 2021 a new tribe within the Baryonychinae, named Ceratosuchopsini, a clade that includes Ceratosuchops, Riparovenator, and Suchomimus.

facts.statement: Suchomimus shared traits with Baryonyx, including strong forelimbs, a huge sickle-curved thumb claw, and strongly keeled front dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Suchomimus was very similar to the spinosaurid Baryonyx from the Barremian of England, and shared traits with it such as the reduced size and increased amount of teeth behind the snout tip in the mandible than spinosaurines, strong forelimbs, a huge sickle-curved claw on its "thumb", and strongly keeled front dorsal vertebrae.

facts.statement: Spinosaurids lived from approximately 130 to 95 million years ago during the Early to Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Spinosaurids appear to have been widespread from the Barremian to the Cenomanian stages of the Cretaceous period, about 130 to 95 million years ago

facts.statement: Suchomimus lived in Africa during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 125 to 112 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 125 a 112 millones de años, en el Aptiense, en lo que hoy es África

facts.statement: Suchomimus possessed a long, narrow, crocodile-like skull with sub-circular teeth that had fine to no serrations.
facts.quote: They shared features such as long, narrow, crocodile-like skulls; sub-circular teeth, with fine to no serrations

facts.statement: Suchomimus had an extensive secondary palate that strengthened the roof of its mouth to resist twisting forces from prey.
facts.quote: Suchomimus's extensive secondary palate, which would have made the roof of the mouth more solid, allowed it to better resist twisting forces exerted by prey

facts.statement: Suchomimus is named for its elongated, shallow skull, which resembles that of a crocodile.
facts.quote: El cráneo alargado y poco profundo de Suchomimus, similar al de un cocodrilo, le otorga su nombre genérico

facts.statement: Suchomimus was named and described by paleontologist Paul Sereno and colleagues in 1998 based on a partial skeleton from the Elrhaz Formation.
facts.quote: Fue nombrado y descrito por el paleontólogo Paul Sereno y colegas en 1998, basándose en un esqueleto parcial de la Formación Elrhaz

facts.statement: The specific name S. tenerensis refers to the Teneré Desert where the first remains of Suchomimus were found.
facts.quote: el nombre específico S. tenerensis alude a la localidad donde fueron encontrados sus primeros restos, el desierto de Teneré

facts.statement: Researchers suggested Suchomimus was a fish-eater based on its elongated jaws, spoon-shaped snout tip, and long teeth similar to those of piscivorous crocodilians.
facts.quote: Sereno and colleagues suggested the same dietary preference for Suchomimus, based on its elongated jaws, spoon-shaped terminal rosette, and long teeth reminiscent of those of piscivorous crocodilians

facts.statement: Isotopic evidence indicates Suchomimus relied heavily on aquatic resources, supporting a semi-aquatic foraging habit.
facts.quote: Isotopic geochemical lines of evidence also support a semi-aquatic foraging habit for Suchomimus; its δ44/42Ca values are highly negative, in contrast to contemporary abelisaurids and carcharodontosaurids, indicating a greater reliance on aquatic resources

facts.statement: Suchomimus was adapted for hunting in shallow water due to hollow bones, unlike Baryonyx and Spinosaurus which could fully submerge and dive.
facts.quote: Suchomimus itself was more adapted to a life hunting in shallow water due to its hollow bones, while Baryonyx and Spinosaurus were capable of fully submerging underwater and diving after prey

facts.statement: Researchers have hypothesized that spinosaurid forelimbs and claws were used for digging water sources, reaching hard-to-access prey, or burrowing to build nests.
facts.quote: In a 2017 review of the family, American paleontologist David Hone and Holtz Jr. also considered possible functions in digging for water sources or hard-to-reach prey, as well as burrowing into soil to construct nests

facts.statement: Suchomimus is classified within the family Spinosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Spinosauridae

facts.statement: Suchomimus belongs to the subfamily Baryonychinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Baryonychinae

facts.statement: Suchomimus is placed in the tribe Ceratosuchopsini.
facts.quote: tribus: Ceratosuchopsini

facts.statement: Suchomimus shared its habitat with abundant crocodylomorphs, including the giant pholidosaur Sarcosuchus imperator and various smaller notosuchians.
facts.quote: Crocodylomorphs were abundant, represented by the giant pholidosaur species Sarcosuchus imperator, as well as small notosuchians like Anatosuchus minor, Araripesuchus wegeneri, and Stolokrosuchus lapparenti

facts.statement: Sereno and colleagues proposed in 1998 that spinosaurid thumb-claws and robust forelimbs evolved in the Middle Jurassic before adaptations for fish-eating appeared.
facts.quote: Sereno and colleagues proposed in 1998 that the large thumb-claw and robust forelimbs of spinosaurids evolved in the Middle Jurassic, before the elongation of the skull and other adaptations related to fish-eating

facts.statement: Buffetaut and Ouaja suggested in 2002 that baryonychines were the ancestors of spinosaurines, which later replaced them in Africa.
facts.quote: In 2002, Buffetaut and Ouaja also suggested that baryonychines could be the ancestors of spinosaurines, which appear to have replaced the former in Africa

facts.statement: Milner suggested in 2003 that spinosaurids originated in Laurasia during the Jurassic and dispersed into Gondwana via the Iberian land bridge.
facts.quote: Milner suggested in 2003 that spinosaurids originated in Laurasia during the Jurassic and dispersed via the Iberian land bridge into Gondwana, where they radiated

facts.statement: Candeiro and colleagues suggested in 2017 that spinosaurids in northern Gondwana were replaced by abelisauroids after the Cenomanian due to environmental changes.
facts.quote: Candeiro and colleagues suggested in 2017 that spinosaurids of northern Gondwana were replaced by other predators, such as abelisauroids, since no definite spinosaurid fossils are known from after the Cenomanian anywhere in the world

facts.statement: The type specimen of Suchomimus was estimated to be between 10.3 and 11 meters long and weigh between 2.7 and 5.2 tonnes.
facts.quote: La longitud del espécimen tipo de Suchomimus, un subadulto, se estimó inicialmente entre 10,3 a 11 metros, con un peso estimado de entre 2,7 y 5,2 toneladas.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated the length of Suchomimus to be 9.5 meters and its weight to be 2.5 tonnes in 2010.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul, sin embargo, dio estimaciones más bajas de 9,5 metros y 2,5 toneladas en 2010.

facts.statement: A 2020 study adjusted the estimated body mass of the holotype to 3.26 tonnes based on femoral circumference.
facts.quote: un estudio de 2020 moderó la masa corporal del holotipo en 3,26 toneladas en función de la circunferencia femoral.

facts.statement: Researchers describe Suchomimus as a large creature that usually ate fish and lived in the Sahara over 100 million years ago when it was a swampy paradise.
facts.quote: La impresión general que plantean los investigadores es la de una criatura de gran porte, que se alimentaba usualmente de peces, y que hace más de 100 millones de años deambulaba por el Sáhara cuando este era un vergel pantanoso.

facts.statement: Unlike other giant theropods, Suchomimus had a very long and low snout formed by the forward expansion of premaxillae, frontal bones, and the posterior ramus of the maxillae.
facts.quote: A diferencia de otros terópodos gigantes tenía un hocico muy largo y bajo, y quijadas estrechas formadas por una expansión hacia adelante de los premaxilares, huesos frontales del hocico y la rama trasera de los maxilares, hueso principal de la mandíbula superior.

facts.statement: Suchomimus jaws were studded with about 120 teeth that were not very sharp, slightly curved backward, and had fine striations and rough enamel.
facts.quote: Las mandíbulas estaban tachonadas con unos 120 dientes no muy agudos y curvados levemente hacia atrás, con finas estrías y esmalte rugoso.

facts.statement: The snout tip was bulbous and carried a rosette of longer teeth, with seven on each side of the premaxillae and approximately the same number on the corresponding part of the lower jaw.
facts.quote: La extremidad del hocico era abultada y llevaba un rosetón de dientes más largos que el resto, siete por lado en los premaxilares y aproximadamente el mismo número en la parte correspondiente de la mandíbula inferior.

facts.statement: Further back, there were at least 22 teeth on each side of the upper jaw in the maxilla, while the entire side of the lower jaw had 32 teeth in the dentary bone.
facts.quote: Más atrás, había al menos 22 dientes por lado de la mandíbula superior en el maxilar superior, mientras que todo el lado de la mandíbula inferior llevaba 32 dientes en el hueso dentario.

facts.statement: Unlike most theropods, the nostrils of Suchomimus were retracted further back in the skull, behind the premaxillary teeth.
facts.quote: Las fosas nasales, a diferencia de la mayoría de los terópodos, estaban retraídas más atrás en el cráneo y detrás de los dientes premaxilares.

facts.statement: The lower jaws were very long and narrow, forming a rigid structure when the dentaries touched in the midline, reinforcing the jaw against torsional forces.
facts.quote: Las mandíbulas inferiores eran muy alargadas y estrechas, formando una estructura rígida cuando sus dentarios se tocaban entre sí en la línea media, reforzando la mandíbula contra las fuerzas de torsión.

facts.statement: Suchomimus had approximately 16 dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Había alrededor de 16 vértebras dorsales.

facts.statement: The neural spines may have supported a low crest or skin sail that was higher over the hips and lower extending toward the back than in Spinosaurus, where the sail reached its highest point over the dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Las espinas pueden haber sostenido una especie de cresta baja o vela de piel que estaba más alta sobre sus caderas, más baja y extendiéndose más hacia la espalda que la de Spinosaurus, en la que la vela alcanzaba su punto más alto sobre las vértebras dorsales.

facts.statement: The arm musculature drove considerable-sized hand claws, with the first digit being the largest at a length of 19 centimeters.
facts.quote: La musculatura del brazo impulsaba garras de mano de tamaño considerables, siendo la del primer dedo la más grande con una longitud de 19 centímetros.

facts.statement: The femur was straight and robust, measuring 107 centimeters in length in the holotype.
facts.quote: El fémur, el hueso del muslo, era recto y robusto, con una longitud de 107 centímetros en el holotipo.

facts.statement: Suchomimus lived over 100 million years ago in the Sahara when it was a swampy paradise.
facts.quote: hace más de 100 millones de años deambulaba por el Sáhara cuando este era un vergel pantanoso.

facts.statement: In 1997, American paleontologist Paul Sereno and his team discovered fossils representing about two-thirds of a large theropod dinosaur skeleton in Niger.
facts.quote: En 1997, después de encontrar nuevos especímenes de Carcharodontosaurus y Sarcosuchus, el paleontólogo estadounidense Paul Sereno y su equipo en Gadoufaoua descubrieron fósiles que representaban aproximadamente dos tercios de un gran esqueleto de dinosaurio terópodo en Níger.

facts.statement: The first find, a giant thumb claw, was made on December 4, 1997, by David Varricchio.
facts.quote: El primer hallazgo, una uña de pulgar gigante, fue realizado el 4 de diciembre de 1997 por David Varricchio.

facts.statement: The specific name tenerensis refers to the Ténéré Desert where the animal was found.
facts.quote: El nombre específico tenerensis se debe al desierto de Ténéré donde se encontró el animal.

facts.statement: The holotype MNN GDF500 is a partial skeleton found in the Tegama Beds of the Elrhaz Formation and lacks a skull.
facts.quote: El holotipo, MNN GDF500, se encontró en los Lechos Tegama de la Formación Elrhaz. Consiste en un esqueleto parcial que carece del cráneo.

facts.statement: The holotype includes neck ribs, parts of dorsal vertebrae and ribs, gastralia, sacral vertebrae, tail vertebrae, chevrons, shoulder girdle bones, a partial forelimb, the pelvis, hip bone, and parts of a hind leg.
facts.quote: Contiene tres costillas del cuello, partes de catorce vértebras dorsales, diez costillas dorsales, gastralias o "costillas del vientre", piezas de tres vértebras sacrales, partes de doce vértebras caudales, cheurones, huesos que forman la parte inferior de la cola, una escápula, un coracoides, una extremidad anterior parcial, la mayor parte de la pelvis, el hueso de la cadera y partes de una pata trasera.

facts.statement: The furcula was described in detail in 2007 after being found during an expedition in 2000.
facts.quote: En 2007, se describió en detalle la fúrcula, encontrada durante una expedición en 2000.

facts.statement: It is debated whether S. tenerensis is a junior synonym of the spinosaurid Cristatusaurus lapparenti from the Elrhaz Formation.
facts.quote: S. tenerensis es potencialmente un sinónimo más moderno de otro espinosáurido de la Formación Elrhaz, Cristatusaurus lapparenti, nombrado el mismo año con base en fragmentos de mandíbula y vértebras.

facts.statement: In 2002, Hans-Dieter Sues and colleagues proposed that Suchomimus is identical to Cristatusaurus lapparenti and should be classified as Baryonyx tenerensis.
facts.quote: En 2002, el paleontólogo alemán Hans-Dieter Sues y sus colegas concluyeron que Suchomimus era idéntico a Cristatusaurus lapparenti y, a pesar de que Cristatusaurus había sido nombrado algo antes que Suchomimus, propusieron que representaran una segunda especie de Baryonyx llamada Baryonyx tenerensis.

facts.statement: In 2021, Barker et al. placed Suchomimus in the new tribe Ceratosuchopsini, separate from Baryonyx, though they did not name Cristatusaurus.
facts.quote: En 2021 Barker et. al. agruparon a Suchomimus en una nueva tribu llamada Ceratosuchopsini, junto a los recién descritos Ceratosuchops inferodios y Riparovenator milnerae, separado a su vez de Baryonyx walkeri, por lo que lo consideran un género separado, aunque no nombran a Cristatusaurus.

facts.statement: Suchomimus belongs to the parent group Ceratosuchopsini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ceratosuchopsini

facts.statement: Suchomimus is classified in the family Spinosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Spinosauridae

facts.statement: Suchomimus lived from the Aptian to the Albian stages, between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Albian (121.4 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: In 1998, Sereno and colleagues suggested Suchomimus had a piscivorous diet based on its elongated jaws, spoon-shaped terminal rosette, and long crocodile-like teeth.
facts.quote: En 1998, Sereno y sus colegas sugirieron la misma preferencia dietética para Suchomimus, basándose en sus mandíbulas alargadas, roseta terminal en forma de cuchara y dientes largos que recuerdan a los de los cocodrilos piscívoros.

facts.statement: Suchomimus had an extensive secondary palate that would have strengthened the roof of the mouth to resist torsion forces from prey.
facts.quote: El extenso paladar secundario de Suchomimus, que habría hecho más sólido el techo de la boca, lo que le permitía resistir mejor las fuerzas de torsión ejercidas por la presa.

facts.statement: The discovery of Suchomimus revealed that spinosaurid skulls were significantly shallower, longer, and narrower than previously thought.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento de Suchomimus reveló que los cráneos de los espinosáuridos eran significativamente menos profundos, más alargados y estrechos de lo que se pensaba.

facts.statement: The function of the robust forelimbs and giant claws of spinosaurids remains a debated topic.
facts.quote: El uso de las extremidades anteriores robustas y las garras gigantes de los espinosáuridos sigue siendo un tema debatido.

facts.statement: In 1986, Charig and Milner speculated that Baryonyx might have crouched by the riverbank and used its claws to pull fish from the water, similar to grizzly bears.
facts.quote: En 1986 que Baryonyx pudo haberse agachado junto a la orilla del río y usaba sus garras para sacar peces del agua, de manera similar a los osos Grizzly.

facts.statement: In 2005, François Therrien and colleagues hypothesized that spinosaurid forelimbs were likely used to hunt larger prey because their snouts could not withstand bending tension.
facts.quote: Un estudio de 2005 realizado por el paleontólogo canadiense François Therrien y sus colegas postuló que las extremidades anteriores de los espinosáuridos probablemente se usaron para cazar presas más grandes, dado que sus hocicos no podían resistir la tensión de flexión.

facts.statement: In a 2017 family review, David Hone and Holtz considered possible functions for spinosaurid forelimbs in digging for water sources, hard-to-reach prey, or excavating nests.
facts.quote: En una revisión de la familia de 2017, David Hone y Holtz también consideraron posibles funciones en la excavación de fuentes de agua o presas difíciles de alcanzar, así como en la excavación en el suelo para construir nidos.
